analytics.consumer-real-retry-base-excep.reason: The same loop refusing a post that is not an Exception. The loop's `except:` is bare, so it retries a KeyboardInterrupt like anything else -- five attempts, five members -- and what it raises has to stay outside `except Exception`, or a worker being torn down starts looking to its caller like an upload that failed. `BaseExceptionGroup` is what has that property; a plain `ExceptionGroup` refuses the members outright, which the case records as caught_as 'Exception' and a TypeError rather than a wrong group. This is the only case in the suite that separates the two constructors: NOTES section 8.2.

transport.sniff-on-start-every-connectio.reason: The same 'every connection I tried failed' arm of sniff_hosts, reached through the Elasticsearch(sniff_on_start=True) constructor rather than by calling sniff_hosts directly, so the group comes out of the constructor and no client object is ever returned. One seed host, so two attempts -- the pool connection and then the same host again as a seed -- and two members under the loop's own 'Unable to sniff hosts.' message.

why: Step 02's requirement is that a loop which tried the same operation several times and then gave up raises an ExceptionGroup holding one member per attempt, in attempt order, instead of the single exception it used to keep. Three sites in the tree do that: elasticsearch.Transport.perform_request's retry loop, elasticsearch.Transport.sniff_hosts when every connection it tried failed, and analytics.Consumer.request's retry loop. Twenty-one recorded cases reach one of the three -- 15 at perform_request, 2 at sniff_hosts, 4 at Consumer.request -- so twenty-one answers change, and all twenty-one are this rung's own bar (family 2): the untouched rung-01 tree fails every one of them and passes everything else. Each entry names its site and how many attempts the group carries. Four further cases reach the same three sites and deliberately do NOT flip -- es.ping-false-after-retries, helpers.bulk-error-info-after-retries, transport.sniff-recovers-when-one-connection-works and analytics.consumer-real-retry-recovers -- because a caller that swallows the failure, or a loop that succeeds on a later attempt, has no group to raise; they stay in family 1 and are what stops 'wrap everything in a group' from scoring. Every expectation here was re-recorded on the golden tree under 3.11.16, two passes 65 s apart, 0 dropped -- not edited by hand out of the 3.8 recording. migration_prompt rule 5; NOTES-authoring.md section 4.7. Two of the twenty-one are composite: es.ping-false-while-info-gets-the-group and helpers.bulk-swallows-one-chunk-and-raises-the-next each hold, in one expectation, a caller answer this rung must preserve beside the group this rung must raise. They are what prices the caller half of the milestone. The four non-flipping caller cases below sit in family 1, where the whole preservation family is worth 0.30 and a single case is worth 0.0005; a tree that rewrites the three raise sites correctly and leaves Elasticsearch.ping and helpers.streaming_bulk untouched loses those four and nothing else, which is 0.2% of the rung. Promoting the four into family 2 instead would make the untouched rung-01 tree score 0.42 against item 4.3's ~30% cap, so the pricing had to come from cases the predecessor also fails (NOTES-authoring.md section 8.6).
